paper_title: DTaPO: Dynamic Thermal-Aware Performance Optimization for Dark Silicon Many-Core Systems

scenario.figure_or_table: Section 4.1 and Table 4; Figure 10 (slowdown and Tmax/Tavg/Tmin across DTM techniques and thresholds); Figure 4 (floorplan)
scenario.description: DTaPO (task migration plus DVFS) evaluated on a simulated 64-core NoC many-core system, with 32 active and 32 dark cores in a chessboard pattern. The workload mixes radix, ocean, blackscholes and bodytrack with 8 threads each. Thresholds range from 60 to 85 C, compared against DVFS-only and no-DTM baselines. Core size is 2.95 mm x 2.95 mm. No per-core power values or absolute core coordinates are published in the paper text.
scenario.architecture: 64-core homogeneous 22 nm NoC many-core (8x8 mesh, 4 GHz max, 32 KB L1-I/L1-D, 512 KB L2 per core, 8 MB L3 per 8 cores), 2D planar die, HotSpot ceramic BGA package stack with heat spreader and heat sink
scenario.workload: Mix of Splash-2 radix and ocean and PARSEC blackscholes and bodytrack, 8 threads each, run on 32 active cores
scenario.operating_point: Threshold temperatures 60-85 C (epsilon 5 C, frequency step 200 MHz, Fthr 3.6 GHz), ambient 318.15 K, 50% dark silicon

original_setup.solver: LifeSim toolchain: Sniper performance simulation, McPAT power estimation (22 nm), and HotSpot (HotSpot 6.0 cited) transient thermal simulation with a stacked ceramic BGA package model (Section 4.1, PDF pp. 8-10, Table 4 on p. 11)
original_setup.optimizer: No formal numerical optimizer. DTaPO is a heuristic runtime algorithm (Algorithm 1, p. 8) that minimizes makespan subject to Ti < Tthr for all cores (Eq. 3, p. 7). Parameters epsilon = 5 C, frequency step = 200 MHz and Fthr = 3.6 GHz were set empirically (p. 10).
original_setup.controller: DTaPO: periodic threshold-based dynamic thermal management. It sees transient core temperatures, migrates tasks one way from hot active cores to cooler dark cores within an LLC-sharing cluster, and falls back to stepwise DVFS when no cooler core is available. The 64 cores sit in an 8x8 mesh with a 50% chessboard active/dark pattern (pp. 5-8).
original_setup.benchmark: 64-core 22 nm NoC many-core system with 32 active and 32 dark cores. Workload mix: Splash-2 radix and ocean plus PARSEC blackscholes and bodytrack, 8 threads each (Table 3, p. 10). Thresholds 60-85 C are compared against DVFS-only and no-DTM baselines (Figure 10, p. 13). A separate 10-application comparison against OSP uses TDP = 42 W (Figure 12, p. 15).

thermal_observable.unit: degC (reduction in average peak temperature of DTaPO relative to DVFS-only; a delta, not an absolute temperature)
thermal_observable.location: Per-core transient temperatures of the simulated 64-core chip, with peak taken over the cores. The paper states the maximum and minimum are represented by the 90th and 10th percentiles of the fluctuating transient temperatures.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Average of 10 repeated runs over the four-application mix, with the reduction reported as the maximum across thresholds (60-85 C). Text on p. 15 and abstract p. 1; per-threshold Tmax/Tavg/Tmin bars are shown in Figure 10 (p. 13) and have not been digitized. A separate 13.6 degC peak reduction vs OSP is reported for the 10-application comparison.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper's result depends on dynamic transient control: closed-loop DTaPO task migration and DVFS, with a 100 us wake-up latency, 1000-cycle migration penalty and cache cold-start effects. A steady-state 2D Studio solve with a fixed placement and a one-row power trace cannot reproduce the controller behavior or the dynamic thermal results.

The paper publishes no per-core or per-block power values, only that McPAT was used. Per-core power cannot be split from a total, since no total chip power or splitting rule is given. Core absolute coordinates are also not published; only the core size (2.95 mm x 2.95 mm) and the chessboard pattern are given.

The paper's solver is the coupled Sniper/McPAT/HotSpot/LifeSim toolchain with a CBGA package: heat spreader, heat sink with R = 0.1 K/W, TIM, ceramic substrate and printed board. A Studio solver with different package/cooling assumptions would not match it. The 3D, interposer and chiplet aspects are not applicable, because the paper uses a monolithic 2D planar die.

The optimizer and workload are architecture-level: DVFS levels, task mapping and multi-threaded benchmarks over time-varying power. No optimizer is involved in the Studio setup and no placement optimization is performed. The paper also covers no reliability analysis and no 3D stacking.

missing_inputs: No paper-linked URLs, repositories, supplementary data or code were found (artifact search: checked, no links); the packet contains no pinned assets (assets array empty), so no config, floorplan or thermal-config files could be inspected.
Per-core power values in W (McPAT outputs) and power time series or traces are not published.
Absolute x_m and y_m placement coordinates of the cores (Figure 4 shows only a schematic floorplan) are missing.
Chip total die dimensions and the L3 cache block size and location are not given.
The HotSpot floorplan, HotSpot control period, and package dimensions (spreader and sink area) are missing; Table 4 gives only material and convection parameters.
Digitized numerical values of Tmax/Tavg/Tmin per threshold from Figure 10 and the transient traces from Figure 11 are not provided.
Details of the Studio package and material assumptions bundled with the runner were not supplied in the packet.
